clue.text: Steamship taking this time to float into frozen hazards

indicators.note: a ship taking something on board holds it within its hull, so the other words go inside

blocks.note: SS is the standard abbreviation for a steamship

explanation.surface: A steamer steering off course into dangerous ice and snow in polar waters.
explanation.walkthrough: The two letters of the ship's abbreviation split to wrap around the time word and the floating word.
explanation.definitionFit: Banks of snow heaped by wind block roads and paths, making them winter obstacles for travellers.

clue.text: Speak with force like Hook, for example

blocks.note: as means in the manner of
Captain Hook is the pirate in Peter Pan

explanation.surface: Someone declaiming theatrically in the manner of Captain Hook.
explanation.walkthrough: To aspirate is to sound a breathy H, the very letter Hook begins with.
explanation.definitionFit: Phonetically, an aspirated sound is uttered with an audible puff of breath, a forceful exhalation.

clue.text: Graduate thus starting to study the fundamentals

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: a Bachelor of Arts is a graduate
Latin for thus, as printed in quotations

explanation.surface: A new graduate beginning to study the essentials of a subject.
explanation.definitionFit: Basics are the elementary principles of anything, the core essentials one learns first.

clue.text: Past generation initially impatient to get going

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the word it follows

explanation.surface: An older generation was once eager to set off and make changes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone agog is eagerly excited and keen, waiting expectantly for something to begin.

clue.text: Bach said to be on a roll with composer's penultimate boat song

indicators.note: said tells us to take the composer's name as it is pronounced, not spelt
penultimate means next to last, so one letter just before the end is kept

blocks.note: the German composer's name said in British fashion sounds like a dog's bark
the letter before the final r of composer

explanation.surface: A composer on a winning streak, the penultimate piece being a boat song.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech Bach is said like bark.
explanation.definitionFit: A barcarolle is a Venetian gondolier's song, or music written in imitation of its rocking rhythm.

clue.text: The last people to get drinks?

blocks.note: first meaning: shoemakers, who shape shoes on a last
second meaning: iced drinks of wine or sherry with fruit and sugar

explanation.surface: Whoever is last in line at the bar is the last to be served.
explanation.walkthrough: The last looks like the end of a queue; it is the wooden foot a shoemaker works on.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoe repairers work on a last, and a sherry cobbler is an iced mixed drink.

clue.text: Indian born to pussyfoot?

blocks.note: a pussy's foot is a paw
née marks a maiden name: born

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone from India was born to tread cautiously.
explanation.walkthrough: Pussyfoot looks like a verb meaning to be evasive; read it as a cat's foot. Born is added to it, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pawnee are a Native American people of the Great Plains, once called American Indians.

clue.text: "A pathological sac", said Sister, with no hesitation

indicators.note: said indicates the remaining word counts for its sound, not its spelling
with no means the following item is taken away

blocks.note: er is the sound of hesitation
what is left of the nursing title, spoken

explanation.surface: A ward sister defining a medical term crisply and without hesitating.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping ER from SISTER leaves SIST, which sounds the same as CYST.
explanation.definitionFit: A cyst is an abnormal closed sac in body tissue, filled with fluid or semi-solid matter.

clue.text: No way! A trainee soldier needs one for remembrance

blocks.note: a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An outraged denial, then a recruit who needs one for a memorial service.
explanation.walkthrough: No way! reads as an exclamation, but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Nostalgia is wistful longing for the past, a fond recollection of earlier times.

clue.text: Egg producer wants nothing to change

explanation.surface: A hen, perhaps, that wants nothing in its life to change.
explanation.definitionFit: An ovary is the female reproductive organ in which ova, or egg cells, are formed.

clue.text: Hand that's straightening things out, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly signals that the word is heard rather than read

explanation.surface: A helping hand that sorts out everyone's problems.
explanation.walkthrough: Hand looks like a helper; it is a person's handwriting.
explanation.definitionFit: Your hand is your style of penmanship, so the script you produce on paper.

clue.text: Storage space for the ministers

blocks.note: first meaning: a cupboard with shelves or drawers
second meaning: the senior government ministers as a body

explanation.surface: Finding room in government buildings for ministers to keep their papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabinet is a piece of furniture with drawers, and also the group of senior ministers advising a prime minister.

clue.text: Papers resorting to smear tactics?

indicators.note: re-sorting means sorting again, putting letters into a fresh order
tactics are manoeuvres, so the letters are moved about

explanation.surface: Newspapers falling back on dirty campaigns of character assassination.
explanation.walkthrough: Papers looks like the press, but it is quantities of paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A ream is a quantity of paper, nominally 500 sheets, so reams are large amounts of paper.

clue.text: Eager to change fellows thought at first to be in accord

indicators.note: a word made to change is rearranged into another
at first points to a word's opening letter only

explanation.surface: People keen to change their views until everyone sees eye to eye.
explanation.definitionFit: An accord is a formal settlement between parties, the same thing as a pact or treaty.

clue.text: Staff supplies found after plane crash

indicators.note: a crash smashes things up, leaving the letters jumbled

blocks.note: stock is a store of goods

explanation.surface: Crew and provisions recovered from the wreckage of a downed aircraft.
explanation.walkthrough: Staff looks like crew members, but it is a walking stick.
explanation.definitionFit: An alpenstock is a long iron-tipped staff used by mountain walkers and climbers.

clue.text: Drunk stays below, where few can walk straight lines

definitions.text: where few can walk straight lines

blocks.note: stays are ropes supporting a mast

explanation.surface: A drunk staying downstairs, unable to walk in a straight line.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue the second piece sits below the first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tightropes are taut wires for balancing acts, which only skilled funambulists can cross on foot.

clue.text: People from Calais and Cracow join in grand wood activity

blocks.note: G is short for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: Visitors from France and Poland meeting for a grand outing in the forest.
explanation.walkthrough: People from serves both cities: one gives the nationality, the other the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: French polishing is a technique of finishing furniture with shellac to give timber a high gloss.

clue.text: I take chances around bends

indicators.note: turned around suggests the letters are shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: A racing driver confessing to risky driving on twisting corners.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicanes are sharp double turns built into motor-racing circuits to slow cars down.

clue.text: Incorruptible? I'm only human!

blocks.note: a mortal is a human being, bound to die

explanation.surface: Someone tempted by a bribe pleads ordinary human weakness.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the wordplay says I am mortal while the answer means the reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: The immortal cannot decay or perish, which is the old physical sense of incorruptible.

clue.text: Pass judgement on one held inside with sensitivity

indicators.note: held inside means enclosed within the other piece

blocks.note: to sentence is to pass judgement

explanation.surface: A judge sentencing a prisoner held in custody, but compassionately.
explanation.definitionFit: Sentience is the capacity to feel and perceive, a responsiveness to sensation.

clue.text: Partners inside only changed leg wear

indicators.note: a word changed has its letters reordered
inside places the following letters within the partners

blocks.note: North and South are bridge partners

explanation.surface: Couples who only changed into different stockings.
explanation.walkthrough: At bridge North and South play as partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Nylons are women's stockings or tights, made from the synthetic fibre of that name.

clue.text: Office worker with time to prepare lure

blocks.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A temporary secretary given time to set out bait.
explanation.definitionFit: To tempt someone is to entice or attract them towards something desirable.

clue.text: This includes points for a dissertation

indicators.note: includes means holds the next item within it

blocks.note: east and south are compass points

explanation.surface: A student pointing to the key arguments within a long essay.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is the long research essay written for a university degree.

clue.text: Fifty hold out after sailor returns with iron pigs

indicators.note: a sailor who returns heads back the way he came, so the word runs backwards
after places the fifty and hold out pieces second, behind the sailor

explanation.surface: Fifty men holding out until a sailor returns with iron ingots.
explanation.walkthrough: Pigs here are oblong castings of crude iron, not animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Ships used pig iron as ballast, heavy weight stowed low in the hull for stability.

clue.text: Little one is produced by degrees

explanation.surface: A child brought into being by qualifications, as if academics bred.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural degrees supplies two qualifications, each two letters long.
explanation.definitionFit: A babe is a baby or infant, a very young child.

clue.text: Goodbye, little sausage!

blocks.note: first meaning: an informal British farewell
second meaning: a small cocktail sausage, as known in New Zealand

explanation.surface: Bidding farewell to a small sausage.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is a casual parting salutation, and in New Zealand also names a small red frankfurter.

clue.text: Council's top social worker is not able to

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its first letter

blocks.note: ants are social insects and worker ants exist

explanation.surface: The head of a council's social services is unable to help.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker looks like a caseworker; it is an insect living in colonies.
explanation.definitionFit: The contraction of cannot expresses inability, matching being unable to do something.

clue.text: Bender being moved?

indicators.note: something moved is shifted about, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is someone who is moved emotionally the type to bend?
explanation.walkthrough: A bender is British slang for a drinking spree, not something that bends.
explanation.definitionFit: A binge is a spell of excessive drinking or indulgence, the same as going on a spree.

clue.text: Frank dined with the contestant

explanation.surface: A man named Frank had dinner with a competitor.
explanation.walkthrough: Frank looks like a man's name; it is the adjective for honest.
explanation.definitionFit: A candidate is someone standing for election or competing for a position or prize.
